## How do I connect an AI model?

<a id="connect-ai"></a>

Open AI & Automation and pick one of two choices: a free model on this computer (nothing leaves your PC), or your ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan (sign in in your browser; no API key and no extra bill). You can use both.

**Where:** **Setup › AI & Automation** (`/ai-settings`)

1. Open AI & Automation (Company > AI & Automation). → **Setup › AI & Automation** (`/ai-settings`)
2. Free, on this computer: click "Set up free AI on this computer". On Windows Ironbooks installs Ollama, downloads a starter model and connects it.
3. Your subscription: click "Continue with ChatGPT" and sign in in your browser. Then turn on "Allow cloud AI for this company".
4. Click "Test connection". Ask AI and the automatic suggestions now use your model.

> Good to know: With both set up, the local model answers first and ChatGPT takes over when it cannot.
>
> Good to know: Other services (Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek, Azure OpenAI, any OpenAI-compatible server) are under "Add AI…" with an API key, billed by that service per use.
>
> Good to know: A model on another computer of yours: "Find models on other computers (Tailscale)".

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I connect an AI model?", or ask Ask AI.*

## What can I ask Ask AI?

<a id="ask-ai"></a>

Click Ask AI in the top bar and ask in plain words. It answers questions about your numbers from your own reports, tells you how to do something and links to the screen, and can draft an entry for you to approve. It never changes your books on its own.

**Where:** **Ask AI** (`/dashboard?assistant=1`)

1. Numbers: "How did we do this month?", "Who owes us money?", "What is our cash balance?". Each figure names the report it came from.
2. How-to: "How do I reconcile my bank account?", "Where do I enter a bill?". The answer comes with a button that opens the screen.
3. Recording: "Record a $120 bill from Office Supply Co for supplies". It prepares a bill, invoice, payment or journal entry and shows it for you to Approve or Reject.

> Good to know: Without a connected model Ask AI still gives basic answers from your reports and the built-in guide.
>
> Good to know: With a cloud model, listed names and identifiers are hidden before anything is sent.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "What can I ask Ask AI?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I let an AI agent work in my books?

<a id="set-up-an-agent"></a>

An Admin adds the agent in Users & Roles > Agents, the way you would add a bookkeeper: a name, a role and what it may do without asking. Ironbooks then shows the agent's access token once, with the settings to paste into Claude Code or Claude Desktop.

**Where:** **Setup › Users & Roles** (`/users`)

1. On the computer that holds the company file, open Users & Roles and click the Agents tab. → **Setup › Users & Roles** (`/users`)
2. Click "New agent". Give it a Name: it is shown in the audit trail next to everything the agent does.
3. Tick a Role. The agent sees what a person with that role sees and can never ask for more. Choose the smallest role that does the job.
4. Under "What it may do without asking", keep "Ask for every change" unless you have a reason to change it: the agent then looks and prepares drafts by itself, and every change to the books waits for a person to say yes.
5. Leave "May work while nobody is signed in" off unless the agent must work when nobody is at the computer. Click "Make agent".
6. Copy what the next window shows: the Access token, and the line for Claude Code or the block for Claude Desktop. The token is shown only now. Keep it like a password, then click "I have copied it".
7. Paste the settings into Claude Code or Claude Desktop on this computer. The agent works while the company file is open here and someone has signed in. What it asks for waits in Agent requests. → **Agent requests** (`/agent-requests`)
8. To change what it may do later, click the agent in the list. "Pause this agent" stops it at once; Remove takes its access away for good.

> Good to know: Only an Admin can add or remove an agent, or let one do more by itself. Whoever may change users can make an agent stricter, pause it, or revoke standing permission it was given.
>
> Good to know: An agent never changes its own settings or another agent's, never approves its own requests, and may not change or delete a role an agent holds.
>
> Good to know: What an agent reads is sent to the AI service that runs it. With an AI model on your own computer or network, nothing leaves.
>
> Good to know: Full Social Security and account numbers are never shown to an agent unless a person approves that one request. The Audit Trail says what was shown, to which agent, and who approved it.
>
> Good to know: A lost token cannot be shown again: remove the agent and make a new one. An Admin can stop every agent at once with "Pause all agents".

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I let an AI agent work in my books?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I approve or deny what an agent asks to do?

<a id="approve-agent-requests"></a>

What an agent's settings say to ask for waits in Agent requests. Open a request, check what Ironbooks worked out it would do, then choose "Approve once", "Approve similar…" or "Deny…".

**Where:** **Agent requests** (`/agent-requests`)

1. When an agent asks, a number shows on "Agent requests" in the left menu (in the desktop app, also at the top of the window). → **Agent requests** (`/agent-requests`)
2. Click Open on a request. The card shows the agent's reason in quotes (its own words, which Ironbooks has not checked) and what the request would do: the entries it would post, what it would change, any email, file or printing, and any warnings.
3. If it is right, click "Approve once". Ironbooks does it now, with your access.
4. To let the agent do requests like this one by itself for a while, click "Approve similar…", choose "For how long" and the limits under "Only when", then click "Approve this and similar".
5. If it is not right, click "Deny…", write a note for the agent if you like, and click "Deny request". Nothing is done.
6. Several requests of the same kind can be approved together: tick them, click "Approve chosen (…)…", check the list and the total it shows, and approve.

> Good to know: "The books changed since the agent asked" means someone changed a record the request uses. The card shows what would happen now; approve it only if that is still right.
>
> Good to know: Standing permission lasts until the end of the day at most, and 30 minutes for emails and printing. It is never given for deleting, closed periods, settings, users, the company file, passwords or showing full numbers: those are asked one at a time.
>
> Good to know: Some requests need an Admin, a second person or a password; the card says so. A password typed on the card goes to Ironbooks only, never to the agent.
>
> Good to know: Requests approved together are added up per agent: when they pass the amount above which that agent needs two people, approve them one at a time.
>
> Good to know: Everything an agent did or asked is kept: see the Audit Trail, or Reports > Accountant & Taxes > Agent Activity.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I approve or deny what an agent asks to do?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I let AI categorize bank transactions, and check what it did?

<a id="ai-auto-categorize"></a>

Ironbooks learns how you categorize. It can add the bank lines it is confident about on its own, and you can see and undo every one.

**Where:** **Setup › AI & Automation** (`/ai-settings`)

1. Open AI & Automation. Under Automation, turn "Auto-categorize confident bank-feed transactions" on or off and set the Confidence threshold. → **Setup › AI & Automation** (`/ai-settings`)
2. Open "What the AI posted" to see every line it added, and undo any of them. → **What the AI posted** (`/ai-posts`)
3. Lines below the threshold wait for you in Review bank transactions. → **Banking › Review bank transactions** (`/bank-review`)

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I let AI categorize bank transactions, and check what it did?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I have my books checked for mistakes?

<a id="error-review"></a>

Error Review looks for unbalanced, duplicate and miscategorized entries and other common problems, and explains how to fix each one.

**Where:** **Reports › Error Review** (`/errors`)

1. Open Error Review. → **Reports › Error Review** (`/errors`)
2. Open an issue to read the Analysis, the "Steps to resolve" and the "Impact if unresolved".
3. Fix it where it says, or apply the suggested correction when one is offered.

> Good to know: Data Integrity proves the ledger itself balances: see "How do I check that my data is sound?".

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I have my books checked for mistakes?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I enter things by typing a sentence?

<a id="command-bar"></a>

Press Ctrl+K and type what you want, such as "invoice Acme 3 hours consulting". The form opens filled in for you to check. Nothing is saved without you.

1. Press Ctrl+K anywhere.
2. Type the task: "invoice Acme 3 hours consulting", "show unpaid bills over 60 days", "what did we spend on fuel in Q3?".
3. Check the form that opens and save it yourself.

> Good to know: Common phrases work with no AI model. Sentences the command bar does not recognize are passed to your connected model.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I enter things by typing a sentence?", or ask Ask AI.*
